query: FeNiCrCoCu is considered promising for high-heat wear-resistant use and is suitable for thin-film applications; because bulk preparation is expensive, applying it as a coating on a conventional metal is more practical. Earlier studies reported improved wear or mechanical performance from high-entropy-alloy coatings on Al, Ni, and titanium-alloy substrates, and simulations of FeNiCrCoCu on Cu indicated that sliding speed affects tangential and normal forces. Other work associated composition and grain size with changes in wear damage. However, most prior studies examined a limited operating regime or the properties of the alloys themselves rather than the overall wear resistance of coatings under varied thermal conditions. Subject to retaining FeNiCrCoCu as a coating on a Cu matrix, what single intervention could improve its overall wear resistance during sliding across varied thermal and contact regimes? Present one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its causal mechanism, the predicted outcome relative to an unchanged coating in matched tests, the boundaries within which it should hold, supporting evidence from the introduction, and an experiment with a clear rejection criterion for both the predicted outcome and the proposed mechanism.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of Mo to high-entropy alloy coatings improves their wear resistance by harmonizing hardness and fracture toughness.
generation.boundary: Within the range of Mo contents investigated
generation.uncertainty: Limited operating regime and properties of the alloys themselves
generation.falsification_experiment: Investigate the tribological properties of the material with different Mo contents

cited_evidence.text: In recent years, high-entropy alloy coatings (HEA) have attracted significant attention due to their unique design concept and excellent comprehensive performance [,]. On that basis, the high-entropy ceramics coatings (HEC) are formed by filling nitrogen atoms in the interstitial position of high-entropy alloy coatings, which process a stronger lattice distortion effect which leads to better mechanical properties [,]. Excellent mechanical properties make high-entropy ceramics coatings a potential candidate for wear-resistant materials []. The objective of this study is to investigate how the addition of the lubricating element Mo harmonizes the hardness and fracture toughness and thereafter affects the tribological properties of the material. To do that, a series of (AlCrTiZrMox)N coatings with different Mo contents were deposited using magnetron co-sputtering. The elemental composition, microstructure, mechanical properties, and tribological properties of the coatings were investigated, and the relationship between the wear resistance and the mechanical properties of the coatings was revealed.
